runs.name: The 2x2 declarative sweep, end to end
runs.description: The main event: smoke test, generate all four cells, train the 2x2 comparison, score the companion thresholds. One button, about four and a half hours, no parameters -- every path in it is a literal. It regenerates the four cells every time, even when they are already on disk, which costs about 25 minutes and buys an entry with no hidden prerequisite; generation is deterministic, so it rewrites the same bytes. If the cells are already there and only the training needs repeating -- a comparison that failed at hour three, say -- use 'Declarative sweep: compare the four cells' instead.

runs.name: The register-arm sweep, end to end
runs.description: Prediction 6 in one button: smoke test, generate the three cells at companion 0.5 with declarative 0.0, 0.3 and 0.6, train the register comparison, score the companion thresholds. About three and a half hours, no parameters. Two of its three cells are also written by the 2x2 sweep; regenerating them here is deliberate and harmless, because generation is deterministic from the seed, salt, fold and split, so the second write produces byte-identical files and the entry carries no hidden prerequisite. If the cells exist and only the training needs repeating, use 'Declarative sweep: compare 0.3 against 0.6 (the register arm)' instead.

runs.name: Lexical variant expansion: the 2x2, end to end
runs.description: Task 6 of the lexical variant expansion plan, as one button: smoke test, generate the clean fever tree, expand it at the operating point the rule-authoring report recommends (rate 0.4 at clean share 0.25, p = 0.30), re-check the rules against the library lint before any GPU time, train the four cells of the 2x2, then compute the paired flip rate for both arms and score the pre-registered decisive-accuracy guard. Twenty trainings -- four cells of five folds -- at roughly ten minutes a cell, so about forty minutes of GPU. Read the pre-registration first: the expected movement on the clean synthetic test set is *nothing*, and a large gain there is evidence of a new shortcut rather than a removed one. Both expansion steps pin `--rules signal`, so this entry stays the v1 arm -- the 2026-09-04 anchor -- byte for byte once swap-class files exist on disk. Every path is a literal and the entry takes no parameters.
step_labels: Check the rules against the library lint
Cell 2: clean-trained, expanded test (does the fault exist?)
Cell 3: expanded-trained, clean test (the guard cell)
Paired flip rate, both arms, and the guard

runs.name: Swap classes: the five-arm batch, end to end
runs.description: Task 9 of the lexical variant expansion v2 plan, as one button. Read `reports/encoder_training/2026-09-05-swap-class-preregistration.md` before pressing it: the bounds, the arms and every read-out were fixed before this entry existed, and the decision arm is `combined` -- the other four are exploratory and a positive result in one of them alone is a hypothesis for another night, not a finding. The batch opens with the CUDA smoke test, the dry-run lint over every rule and class file, and the reproduce check (the v1 expansion must print 1.375 substitutions per 100 words and 27,274 changed examples, as it did on 2026-09-04), so a wasted night fails in minute five rather than hour eight. Then one clean tree, four expansions of it at the operating point the v1 run used (rate 0.4, clean share 0.25, seed 42, p = 0.30), thirteen five-fold trainings and four paired flip rates. `--test-dir` is a single path, so an arm scored against two test trees is two invocations that each train their own folds: 65 fold-trainings, about 130 minutes of GPU, of which 25 trainings are the clean arm trained five identical times -- a limitation of the CLI, and the pre-registration reads their agreement as a determinism cross-check. The first cell is the canary: pooled decisive accuracy on the clean test tree must reproduce 0.9329, and a miss stops the night with an environment change the first thing to rule out. Every path is a literal and the entry takes no parameters.

runs.name: CUDA smoke test
runs.description: Torch and the GPU only: a real matmul on the device, plus torch.version.cuda beside the compute capability. Ten seconds, and the first thing to run on a new machine or after any driver or wheel change.

runs.name: Training canary: one signal, one fold
runs.description: The three-minute check that this machine can actually train, as opposed to merely holding a GPU. The smoke test launches a matmul; only a real backward pass catches an op with no deterministic kernel under --determinism strict, an out-of-memory at the configured batch size, or a fused optimiser kernel that faults on a mismatched wheel. Generates its own single-fold tree first -- a fold tree records the fold count it was generated at, so a one-fold run cannot read a cell built at five -- and writes to canary directories of its own, so it touches nothing a sweep reads. The real-text holdout is skipped: the comparisons load and validate it before any GPU work, so checking it here would only cost time. Press this after a driver or wheel change; the sweeps run it themselves.

runs.name: Score the companion thresholds
runs.description: Reads one comparison's six companion-comparison reports back and scores the criterion declared before the run. Pick the report directory the comparison wrote: 'comparison' for the 2x2, 'register' for the register arm. Stdlib only, no GPU, seconds: the cheapest end-to-end check that the console can run something real, and the way to score a run pulled onto another machine.

runs.name: Generate folds for one signal
runs.description: Fifteen generator runs -- three splits for each of five folds -- under one directory, agreeing on the fold count, salt and seed derivation.

runs.name: Merge the six fold trees
runs.description: Reads the six per-signal fold trees and writes one merged tree beside them, ready for joint multi-head training. Nothing is regenerated. Stdlib only.

runs.name: Declarative sweep: generate folds for all six signals
runs.description: The same cell across all six trainable signals, as six steps under one run. recent_uti_present is excluded: its label turns on a 30-day window and six written policy rules, which no declarative frame can state. Stdlib only, no GPU.

runs.name: Declarative sweep: compare the four cells
runs.description: The 2x2 in one report per signal, columns in cell order: control, declarative alone, companions alone, both. Trains all four from scratch -- roughly four hours on a 12GB card -- because the paired statistics can only be computed inside the invocation that produced them. Generate all four cells first. The first --cell is the reference: its tree is what each report's test slice and cluster checks describe.

runs.name: Declarative sweep: compare 0.3 against 0.6 (the register arm)
runs.description: Prediction 6, and the only run that can find the register failure DD8 argues about: three cells at companion 0.5 and declarative 0.0, 0.3, 0.6. If 0.6 wins on real text, DD8's whole argument is wrong. Needs the c0.5-d0.6 cell generated first.
